question: Serious accusations have emerged from Israel and the UN against the UNRWA regarding the 7 October pogrom against the Israeli population. Numerous teachers employed by the UNRWA are said to have publicly praised the massacre and several UNRWA contract staff reportedly participated in it.

One UNRWA employee allegedly kidnapped an Israeli woman, another removed the body of a murdered soldier, while another took part in the massacre in the Be'eri Kibbutz, where 97 people were killed, including dozens of women, children and elderly people. In the wake of these accusations, 13 countries, including the United States, Germany, Italy and France, have suspended funding to UNRWA.

The Commission and the High Representative have indicated their grave concern at the allegations of UNRWA staff involvement in terrorist attacks, condemned Hamas’s attacks on Israel in the strongest terms, and stated that they will consider further steps based on the outcome of the UN’s forthcoming comprehensive investigation into the case.
Given the above, can the High Representative/Vice-President answer the following questions: 1.
Pending the outcome of the investigation, and if it is not completed by the end of February when the next disbursement of funding to UNRWA is scheduled, will funding be suspended?
How much EU funding has been allocated to UNRWA in total since 7 October 2023?
answer: The Commission has engaged with the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA)’s Commissioner-General and welcomed his commitment to tackle the serious issues at stake. The way forward and the measures and procedures for the disbursement of the Commission’s funding for UNRWA was agreed with the Agency on 1 and 6 March 2024.

The Commission requested the following to the Agency: agreement by UNRWA on the three workstreams (the screening of UNRWA staff; system audit; reinforcement of the department of internal investigations and ethics office) and the signature of the EU-UNRWA contribution agreement; declaration in writing by UNRWA that up-to-date, necessary and proportionate information on staff has been shared with host countries and Israel and will be done on a quarterly basis; and the adoption by UNRWA of a concept note detailing how to strengthen the department of internal oversight services, including the establishment of a new neutrality investigation unit and ethics office.

Following UNRWA’s positive engagement and fulfilment of these conditions, the Commission paid a first tranche of EUR 50 million out of the EUR 82 million foreseen for UNRWA for 2024 on 9 March 2024. The second and third tranches of EUR 16 million respectively are subject to the implementation of the agreement with UNRWA and the Agency’s compliance with the agreed conditions and milestones.

Since 7 October 2023, in terms of development fundings, the Commission disbursed EUR 10 million to UNRWA in November 2023, as a top up of the 2023 allocation granted by the budgetary authority. As mentioned above, the Commission also disbursed EUR 50 million on 9 March 2024, as part of the EUR 82 million allocation foreseen for UNRWA for 2024. Since 7 October 2023, the Commission has also allocated funding of EUR 30.
5 million to UNRWA from the humanitarian aid budget for emergency assistance support to civilians in Gaza and the West Bank.

The EU recognises UNRWA’s vital role in the humanitarian response in Gaza and that it also plays a crucial role for stability in the region (1). This was reiterated by the European Council on 21 March 2024, when EU leaders stressed that the services UNRWA provides in Gaza and across the region are essential (2).
